spec_match.rationale: Probes the exact chromestatus algorithm list (ML-KEM-768/1024, ML-DSA-44/65/87, ChaCha20-Poly1305, X-Wing) via the spec's static SubtleCrypto.supports() when present — correctly placed on the interface object, with the Chromium IDL cited — falling back to real generateKey() calls, and honestly reports that X-Wing is listed but unimplemented.

interactive.rationale: A re-run button, a live method-chip row for the six new SubtleCrypto members, and a per-algorithm matrix where every cell is produced by actually calling the API and shows which path produced it.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises supports()-first detection with a generateKey() fallback and the honest X-Wing divergence note; the page delivers exactly that, including per-cell via labels.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers the unflagged browser (all-no matrix with flag note and exact enable steps), records the real per-algorithm error names (TypeError vs NotSupportedError visible in this session), guards supports() with a fallback, and only asserts the X-Wing-absent contract when the gate is enabled.

references.rationale: Links the Chromium subtle_crypto.idl source directly, but like its siblings omits the https://chromestatus.com/feature/5198951632470016 self-heal link.

conformance.rationale: The suite's subtlecrypto-supports-static and supports-returns-boolean assertions mirror this page's headline surface; failures in this unflagged Chromium 141 are the expected absent gate.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 CLI/CDP (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): the matrix auto-ran on load — desktop screenshot shows all six method chips absent, seven honest 'no' rows with real error names, and the '0 of 7' warn status; zero console errors, no unintended failed requests; only the re-run button could not be clicked.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts that detection ran with the supported count, and conditionally asserts the X-Wing-not-implemented contract when the gate is on.

design_system.rationale: Tokenised colours and a proper mobile-safe overflow-wrap table, but the default-visible warn status (--accent-amber on --bg-stone, ~3.5:1) and flagged-path 'supported' pill (--bg-ivory on --accent-emerald, ~4.0:1) miss WCAG AA 4.5:1 at their small bold sizes.

accessibility.rationale: Semantic table with scoped column headers and a caption, role=status aria-live status line, and cell states written as text (supported/no plus error names), not colour alone.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-emulated 360×740 DPR3 measures 0px horizontal overflow — the four-column matrix survives narrow widths via overflow-wrap:anywhere; desktop 1280×800 clean; only the environmental Google Fonts request fails.

openQuestions.title: Add the chromestatus feature link to this page's see-also
openQuestions.detail: Invariant 3 requires the chromestatus.com/feature/5198951632470016 self-heal link on every page; this page cites the Chromium IDL but not the ChromeStatus entry. One-line additive fix shared across the webcrypto set.

openQuestions.title: Fix sub-AA contrast on the warn status and supported pill
openQuestions.detail: The '0 of 7 algorithms available' warn line (--accent-amber on --bg-stone, ~3.5:1 at 0.8rem bold) is the default state every unflagged visitor sees, and pill.yes (--bg-ivory on --accent-emerald, ~4.0:1) appears for flagged visitors — both under AA 4.5:1. --text-black on emerald (5.1:1) and a darker amber resolve it.

openQuestions.title: Verify the supports()-first path in a flagged Chrome 150+
openQuestions.detail: In this unflagged Chromium 141 every cell exercised only the generateKey() fallback (TypeError/NotSupportedError observed). Run once with WebCryptoPQC enabled to confirm cells switch to 'via supports()', the six method chips flip to present, and X-Wing alone reads no.

summary: An exemplary honest feature-detection page: real calls populate every cell, the detection path is disclosed per cell, and the ChromeStatus-vs-Chromium X-Wing divergence is documented rather than papered over. Verified with headless Chromium 141 via CLI/CDP (chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable in this environment): auto-run produced the all-no matrix with real error names, clean console, no unintended failed requests, no overflow on either device class. Open items: chromestatus link, amber/emerald contrast, flagged supports()-path evidence.
